articles.body: 1. Introduction: The Shift from Answering Questions to Taking Action Artificial intelligence has officially breached the perimeter of the chat window. We are rapidly leaving behind the era where AI merely answers text queries, drafts basic emails, or generates isolated code snippets. Today, AI systems are morphing into active, autonomous operational agents capable of directly navigating desktop software, turning rough sketches into physically manufactured objects, and continuously policing their own internal architectures for security breaches. This transition marks a seismic shift in how software is executed, monitored, and scaled.

articles.body: A CTV measurement workflow needs shared definitions before it needs another dashboard. Developers, media operators and sales teams should agree what each event represents, where it comes from and how it can be connected to a business outcome. Without that agreement, a technically correct report can still answer the wrong question. Simplicity Media's measurement service describes reconciling media, web, call and CRM evidence while keeping attribution and incrementality separate. This article turns that principle into a small, illustrative data contract a development team could discuss with its media partner. Disclosure: This promotional article discusses Simplicity Media. The schema and workflow are recommendations, not a description of its private systems or a tested integration.

articles.title: My Invite Gate Held. The Database Had a Side Door.
articles.excerpt: Originally published on meridianbuild.dev, my build log for FastPass, a paid inbox where people pay to reach you and get refunded if you don't reply. A few weeks ago I wrote about how my invite-only g…
articles.body: Originally published on meridianbuild.dev , my build log for FastPass , a paid inbox where people pay to reach you and get refunded if you don't reply. A few weeks ago I wrote about how my invite-only gate lived in the browser on FastPass , and how I moved it to the server. The comments were kind and sharp. One of them basically asked: you locked the front door, but did you check the back door? I hadn't, not properly. The gate lived in Edge Functions, and it was tested there. But Supabase also exposes the database itself to the browser through PostgREST, and what the browser can do there is decided by Row Level Security (RLS). If RLS let a client write a value that the gate trusts, the gate is decoration. On October 27 I checked. It did.

articles.title: Our AI companion's memory search was upside down for four months, and nothing looked broken
articles.excerpt: I build Calla, an AI companion app whose whole pitch is memory: you tell it about your week, close the app, and the next day it still knows your name, your job and the people in your life. For about f…
articles.body: I build Calla, an AI companion app whose whole pitch is memory: you tell it about your week, close the app, and the next day it still knows your name, your job and the people in your life. For about four months, the part of the system that finds the right memory at the right moment was returning the least relevant memories first. Nobody noticed, including me. Here is how that happens, and what I'd tell anyone building long-term memory for an LLM. Memory is three problems, not one "The bot remembers what I said ten minutes ago" says almost nothing. That's the context window: a rolling buffer the model can see. Close the app and many products start the next session with an empty one. Real long-term memory is three separate jobs, and each can fail quietly: Keeping.

articles.title: AI-Generated Mascots vs Developer-Controlled Rive Characters
articles.excerpt: Stop Treating Your App Mascot Like a Video: Build an Interactive Character With Rive AI-generated animation clips are great for demos. But what happens when your app needs skins, levels, emotions, eye…
articles.body: Stop Treating Your App Mascot Like a Video: Build an Interactive Character With Rive AI-generated animation clips are great for demos. But what happens when your app needs skins, levels, emotions, eye tracking, and real-time control? AI-generated mascot animations are everywhere. You can generate a character, create a few animation clips, and integrate them into your React app, mobile application, or SaaS dashboard. For a simple experience, that works. But imagine your product grows. Your mascot now needs to: React to different application states. Change skins without restarting its animation. Display user progression and level-up effects. Control eye direction and facial expressions independently. Respond to taps, achievements, and real-time events. Evolve into different character forms.

articles.title: JavaScript Copy to Clipboard: Build a Kaomoji Picker
articles.excerpt: Want a useful JavaScript copy to clipboard example that goes beyond copying “Hello world”? Let’s build a small kaomoji picker. Click a face, copy the complete expression, and paste it into a message,…
articles.body: Want a useful JavaScript copy to clipboard example that goes beyond copying “Hello world”? Let’s build a small kaomoji picker. Click a face, copy the complete expression, and paste it into a message, document, or comment. No framework, icon library, or build tools required. Kaomoji are text faces such as (＾▽＾) and ʕ•ᴥ•ʔ. They make a good practice project because the interface is simple, while the strings introduce a few real-world details: Unicode characters, backslashes, browser permissions, and accessible feedback. The finished picker has six buttons, a visible focus outline, and a status message. When automatic copying is unavailable, it offers a selected text field for manual copying. The same pattern works for coupon codes, command-line snippets, and invitation links.

articles.title: Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist
articles.excerpt: Techniques included laptop infections, compromised internal tooling, and fake job interviews.
articles.body: The hackers who stole billions of dollars in cryptocurrency from the Binance exchange spent months working on the theft and used both social engineering and novel malware in the process, the company said Tuesday. The heist, which both the FBI and the TRM Security firm attributed to North Korean actors, initially targeted $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance wallets. The exchange has since frozen or intercepted $2.85 billion of that sum. Binance said it has set aside funds required to cover the loss and provided this link to a Proof of Reserves page. The $6.34 billion represents the biggest sum ever targeted in a cryptocurrency theft.

articles.body: This is an image from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope of NGC 4449, one of the dwarf galaxies in the Galaxies Losing Oxygen via Winds (GLOW) study. Researchers found that dwarf galaxies can hold onto only a small fraction of the oxygen made by their stars. NASA, ESA, Hubble Heritage–ESA/Hubble Collaboration, Alessandra Aloisi (STScI, ESA) This photo released on Nov. 2, 2026, showcases NGC  4449, a dwarf irregular. Researchers using NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies — small galaxies containing a few thousand to hundreds of millions of stars — including NGC 4449 and found that much of the oxygen they expected to see is missing. Read more about this mystery. Image credit: NASA, ESA, Hubble Heritage–ESA/Hubble Collaboration, Alessandra Aloisi (STScI, ESA)
